To overcome the challenge, this paper proposes a dual-domain signal fusion adversarial network (DSFAN) based on Vision Transformer. The network is constructed with a parallel feature extractor based on the Vision Transformer. The time domain and frequency domain signal features are integrated considered after parallel extraction and fusion to achieve cross-domain fault diagnosis of bearings. Meanwhile, to enhance the network's ability to extract domain-invariant features, an adversarial training strategy is employed in conjunction with the Wasserstein distance. In order to evaluate the performance of DSFAN, six cross-domain fault diagnosis tasks were conducted for bearing analysis. Compared to other comparison methods, the experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method exhibits superior diagnostic accuracy and domain alignment performance.

articleTitle: A Rotating Machinery Fault Diagnosis Method Based on Recurrence Characteristics and Model-Agnostic Meta-Learning Under Small Sample Conditions
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Hangzhou)
abstract: To solve the problem that traditional deep learning methods for rotating machinery (RM) are difficult to learn effective fault features and consistent prior knowledge when the fault samples are insufficient and large differences in data distribution. We propose a fault diagnosis method for RM under small sample conditions based on the recurrence characteristics (RC) common to RM and combine it with model-agnostic meta-learning (MAML). Experiments on the CWRU bearing dataset and the NGW planetary gearbox dataset are employed to verify the accuracy and effectiveness. The results show that under the conditions of insufficient fault samples and large differences in data distribution, our method can effectively improve the accuracy of fault diagnosis.

articleTitle: Health Prognostics of Multivariate Deteriorating Machinery Considering Unit-to-Unit Variability
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Hangzhou)
abstract: Multivariable deteriorating machinery (MDM) is commonly encountered in modern industrial environments, where its failure can be attributed to the gradual degradation of multiple health indicators (HIs). More and more researchers have directed their attention toward exploring the dependencies among these HIs and establishing multivariate degradation models. Nevertheless, existing methodologies have disregarded the crucial consideration of unit-to-unit variability in MDM's failure. To address this significant gap, this paper introduces a novel multivariate degradation model. The proposed model effectively incorporates both the dependencies among multiple HIs and the individual differences observed in the degradation process of MDM. The proposed approach employs an online updating algorithm to automatically select the optimal degradation model form and parameters for each HI of MDM, thereby acquiring the marginal failure time distributions. Subsequently, time-varying Copulas are employed here to establish connections between the marginal failure time distributions, and form a joint failure time distribution for MDM. The effectiveness of the proposed method was verified through real degradation data obtained from Stirling refrigerators. The results substantiate the accurate failure time prediction capability of the proposed method while accounting for unit-to-unit variability.

articleTitle: Synthetic Data Generation of Complex Machines with Time Series Generative Adversarial Network
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Hangzhou)
abstract: With the development of commercial spaceflight, the hot-fire testing of reusable liquid rocket engines (LREs) has also been growing, leading to a significant increase in the amount of data. However, among this large amount of data, the proportion of fault data is very small, and the coverage of fault modes is limited, which poses a challenge to the development of fault diagnosis systems. In addition, due to the high level of confidentiality of the test data, the data is usually not shared with system developers, which becomes a longstanding obstacle to data-driven research in the space industry. In order to address the shortage of partial data, there is a great deal of research on simulation-based method. But the simulation data generating from models are different from that of real environment, which makes little effort to data-driven anomaly detection research. Thus, we explored how Generative Adversarial Networks (GAN) can be utilized for complementing real datasets with time-dynamic property. At the same time, since the synthetic data has the same characteristics as the real data but does not contain complete information, it opens up the possibility of providing confidential data to system developers. As a specific target, the focus of this paper is on synthesizing time series data. The largest challenge is to ensure that the synthetic data has engineering values, such as the relationships on synthetic sequences should be consistent with the original variables. Especially for LREs, there is a strong correlation between the data monitored by some sensors of some components, which cannot be ignored when performing data analysis. Considering this unique temporal correlation, Time Series Generative Adversarial Network (TimeGAN) with three loss functions for objective optimization is developed for this effort. In addition to generate and discriminate modules in traditional GAN, it contains embedding and recovery modules, and introduces hidden latent. We use TimeGAN to learn a test data containing eight sequences and generate realistic “fake data”. We used autoregressive moving average models to test the residuals of the individual synthetic sequences and the results demonstrate that this method is well suited for data synthesis of sensory data from LREs.

articleTitle: Research on Fault Intelligent Reasoning Based on Time Series Data
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Hangzhou)
abstract: This paper aims to achieve intelligent fault inference based on time series data, accurately locating the time, location, and causes of faults, and providing maintenance suggestions and methods. To achieve this objective, we integrate a comprehensive fault mode base and fault feature base, delving into the intricate correlations between fault symptoms and fault features. Our approach involves meticulously preprocessing the time series data, encompassing feature extraction, feature selection, and rigorous standardization processing to obtain a standardized format feature data. By applying special logical criteria to faults and features, we perform pattern matching between the feature data and the extensive knowledge base. Through the seamless integration of corresponding algorithms and logical processing, we rapidly and precisely identify the fault location linked to various fault symptoms. Additionally, our methodology enables us to infer detailed information about the fault generation process through association relationships. This research introduces a robust and effective framework for intelligent fault inference, providing valuable insights to support timely and accurate maintenance decisions across diverse industries.

articleTitle: Infrared Thermal Imaging-Based Power MOSFET Thermal Resistance Test Method Research
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Hangzhou)
abstract: Based on the high-precision infrared thermal imaging camera, the calibration effect of black paint coating on the emissivity and temperature measurement results was investigated. We developed a set of device junction temperature test schemes with reduced error, utilizing the Infrascope TM-HST hot spot detection system. Experimental tests were conducted to verify the repeatability of the thermal resistance measurement results obtained from the devised scheme. Based on the structure-function theory, the junction temperature drop curve is obtained by using the determined test scheme, and the integral structure function curve of the device is analyzed to determine the thermal resistance parameters of each structural layer of the device under test. The results demonstrate the practicality and effectiveness of using the structure function method to analyze the thermal resistance parameters of power MOSFETs.

articleTitle: Clustering Features of Lithium-Ion Battery Capacity Degradation Curve
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Hangzhou)
abstract: The capacity degradation behavior of lithium-ion batteries is the key object that the battery life management system needs to monitor in real time. Estimating the remaining service time of the battery through battery parameters such as capacity is one of the main tasks of the battery management system. Due to the complex chemical mechanism that causes the capacity decline of lithium batteries and involves many complex reactions, data-driven methods have been receiving extensive attention. Since the decline process of lithium batteries is divided into different stages, each stage presents different characteristics due to its different main reactions, and the data-driven scheme can achieve better results without or with only a small amount of battery-related knowledge. This paper attempts to use an unsupervised clustering algorithm to classify the capacity decline curve of lithium batteries without relying on other parameters to obtain characteristics that have nothing to do with specific batteries. Finally, two types of cluster centers with more obvious characteristics are obtained. Although the cluster centers obtained with the increase of the number of clusters may be closer to some curves, more similar cluster centers will be introduced, resulting in inaccurate classification results.

articleTitle: Avionics Equipment Cable Fault Injection Design and Simulation Testing Validation
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Hangzhou)
abstract: Aircraft cable is an important part of aircraft avionics communication system. It is of great significance to study the reliability and effectiveness of aircraft cable for the whole aircraft system. The distribution of cables in the whole aircraft communication system is very complicated, including many long transmission lines, which puts forward high requirements for the fault detection of the whole aircraft system. Fault injection, as an important part of system development, needs to meet the growing needs of multiple fault testing. It is used to simulate various fault situations that may occur in the system, so as to detect and evaluate the reliability and stability of the system. Aiming at high fault tolerance, high reliability and large capacity aircraft cable fault detection design, this paper proposes a multi-type fault injection based on FPGA chip to simulate the faults of the physical layer and electrical layer of equipment interconnection in avionics system. It can speed up the validity verification of fault injection detection and fault diagnosis method. In this paper, various signal implementation fault injection methods are explained hierarchically, and the Ethernet transmission line is simplified to replace the AXDF transmission line of avionics system to carry out practical tests. From the test data analysis and demonstration, the method meets the needs of various types of fault injection.

articleTitle: A Platform to Verify Life Prediction Algorithms for Spacecraft Complex Equipment
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Hangzhou)
abstract: The reliability and safety of spacecraft equipment are facing great challenges due to the influence of harsh environments and continuous workloads, coupled with the complex structure of spacecraft equipment and the difficulties in fault diagnosis and equipment maintenance, there is an urgent need for health management technology support. In order to realize the life prediction of complex spacecraft equipment, for the needs of versatility and expandability of the life prediction platform, this paper refers to the advanced validation platforms at home and abroad, selects the spacecraft GNC system as the validation object, and adopts the componentized development mode to develop a modular and expandable life prediction algorithm validation platform, which has a reasonable and advanced system architecture and service mode, and provides input information for different types of life prediction algorithms based on the simulation model and degradation principle of GNC system, and provides an algorithm deployment interface to realize flexible algorithm deployment and validation functions. This paper focuses on the life prediction problem of spacecraft complex equipment, systematically researches its service mode and key technology, combines a variety of advanced life prediction methods, develops a verify life prediction platform, verifies the feasibility and effectiveness of the life prediction algorithm, and is of great significance to the health management and life prediction of spacecraft equipment.

articleTitle: A Life Evaluation Method Based on Accelerated Degradation Tests Under Combination of Cycling and Constant Temperature Stresses for Rubber Sealing Rings
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Hangzhou)
abstract: Some rubber sealing rings usually are little key parts used on aircraft equipment, whose failures sometimes decide the life of the equipment. Generally, accelerated degradation tests with single condition such as constant temperature or temperature cyclings are conducted to evaluate the life time for rubber products. In this paper, considering aircraft flight profile, a life evaluation method is proposed based on accelerated degradation tests under combination of cycling and constant temperature stresses for a kind of rubber sealing rings. Basing cumulative damage theory, the comprehensive reaction rate model and the life time model are derived and established, and also, the processes of parameter estimation are illustrated. At last, a data processing example is given on how to use the method to calculate the life time for the rubber sealing rings.

articleTitle: Application of nuclearization free -noise automatic encoder in planetary gear fault diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Hangzhou)
abstract: Use the characteristics of nuclearization of similar data to each other and alien data away from each other to select the best noise rate of versatile automatic encoder. Secondly, the inertial weight and threshold of the hidden layer of the exfoliating automatic encoder is trained layer by layer to build a feature vector set. In terms of state recognition, some feature vectors are randomly selected as inputs. The state recognition model based on the nuclear limit learning machine algorithm is trained through training. Use the DDS power transmission fault diagnosis of the vibration data collected by the planetary gears collected in different states of the planetary gears to verify the effectiveness of the above methods.

articleTitle: Graph Neural Networks with Adaptive Convolutional ARMA Filters for Fault Diagnosis in Mechanical Complex Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Hangzhou)
abstract: Generally, there will be multiple sensors installed on mechanical complex systems, which provide abundant data for fault detection and diagnosis (FDD) and form graphs naturally with sensors as nodes and relations between sensors as edges. Thus, it should be a more natural and effective way to process the data as graphs taking relations into account not just the data itself. Graph neural networks (GNNs) emerging as specialized graph processing algorithms, have been developed and utilized in FDD. However, much of the work uses the same adjacent matrix to propagate information, which ignores the personalized propagation needs in each layer. In order to solve this problem, we propose a novel GNN called adaptive auto-regressive moving average (ADARMA) neural network based on the auto-regressive moving average (ARMA) neural network to adaptively adjust the adjacent matrix during the training process. We evaluate our method on simulated dataset and find in our method better results can be achieved than the baseline methods.

articleTitle: Research on Multi-objective Replacement Strategy for Railway Freight Car Brake Shoes Based on Monte Carlo Simulation
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Hangzhou)
abstract: To solve the problems of railway freight car brake shoe maintenance, a multi-objective replacement strategy of railway freight car brake shoes based on Monte Carlo simulation is proposed. By collecting the historical data of the remaining thickness of the brake shoes of railway freight cars, using the generalized linear mixed effect model to model the degradation law of the brake shoes, and simulating the degradation law of the brake shoes under the maintenance decision conditions based on different maintenance intervals and brake shoes replacement thresholds by Monte Carlo simulation method, five program evaluation indexes are proposed, and the optimal decision is given to the centralized maintenance of the brake shoes based on the weights of different indexes of the program.

articleTitle: Research on Motor Fault Identification Method Based on Vibration Current Multisource Data Fusion and Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Hangzhou)
abstract: Traditional motor fault diagnosis techniques are usually based on a single type of state parameter. However, the monitoring range of a single type of motor state parameters is very limited, and it is difficult to meet the needs of comprehensive fault diagnosis. The purpose of this paper is to propose a fault diagnosis method for typical AC induction motors by fusing two types of parameters, i. e. vibration data and current data, in order to improve the accuracy of diagnosis. Based on the analysis of the basic faults of typical AC asynchronous motors, this paper studies the methods of motor fault feature extraction, including Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) and Hilbert-Huang Transform (HHT). Then, the method of motor multi-sensor parameter fusion is studied, and the realization scheme of data fusion is designed. Convolutional neural network is constructed as a feature fusion tool. The results of fast Fourier transform (FFT) of current data and Hilbert-Huang transform (HHT) of voltage data of different fault types are input into CNN as fault features, and the deep-seated features are extracted by using CNN's feature extraction ability. Finally, the CNN network series Multilayer perceptron (MLP) was constructed to realize fault classification, and the motor fault identification and fault diagnosis were realized based on the motor vibration and current parameters. The results show that the motor fault diagnosis technology based on data fusion can improve the accuracy of diagnosis results, reduce the uncertainty caused by single parameter, and improve the accuracy of motor fault diagnosis.

articleTitle: Investigation of Civil Aircraft Airborne System Integration Test Procedure
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Hangzhou)
abstract: With the increase in the integration and complexity of civil aircraft airborne systems, the integrated, modular and open architecture of airborne systems has become the trend of future development. The reliability integration test process of civil aircraft developed in this work is based on the demand analysis of test, with “failure” as the platform, and “operational reliability, safety” as the core. The operational reliability and safety test requirements are studied from the perspectives of architecture design, fault tolerance mechanism, monitoring and alarming, and quantitative requirements of reliability and safety, etc.. The reliability integration test workflow is formed based on the functional performance integration test in each phase of the system. In order to effectively apply the results of the reliability integration test to achieve the purpose of “process control, problem regression, test closure and design enhancement”, the process also provides for the design feedback technology research of the reliability integration test results. The feedback mechanism has a great effect on improving the reliability level of civil aircraft system integration. Performing the reliability integration test can enhance the safety and operational reliability foundation of civil aircraft, improve the competitiveness of civil aircraft.

articleTitle: Fault Diagnosis Method for Rotating Machinery Based on Attention Adversarial Transfer Networks Under Variable Operating Conditions
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Hangzhou)
abstract: Recently, deep learning-based fault diagnosis methods for rotating machinery have achieved promising classification performance under the independent and identical distribution of training and test data. However, the complex and variable operating conditions, including bearing speed, working load, and load torque, of rotating machinery in practical applications lead to the problem of inconsistent distribution between training and testing data. To address the above issue, an attentional adversarial transfer network is developed to improve the accuracy of rotating machinery fault diagnosis under variable operating conditions by using adversarial transfer learning techniques. First, a feature extractor based on self-normalized convolutional neural networks (SCNN) is constructed to provide effective features for different domains. A lightweight attention layer is further designed to reinforce the structural information in the features while reducing the redundant disturbances. Then, a discriminator based on probability calculation is employed to perform adversarial learning with the feature extractor so as to achieve the alignment of feature distribution between different domains. Finally, an efficient loss function is designed to drive efficient adversarial transfer learning for the whole model. To verify the effectiveness and superiority of the proposal, the Paderborn University (PU) bearing dataset is selected for fault diagnosis experiments, where proposed method achieves an average cross-domain fault diagnosis accuracy of 88.36%. The experimental results indicate that this approach can implement accurate fault identification for rotating machinery under variable operating conditions.

articleTitle: A Study on Iterative Field Testability Evaluation Method Based on Prior Information
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Hangzhou)
abstract: With the increasing application of precision electronic devices relying on Built-In Test (BIT) in advanced military aircrafts, testability indicators have become an important factor affecting flight safety and generation combat capacity. An iterative field testability evaluation method based on prior information was proposed under the Bayesian framework to deal with the problems of few testability evaluation samples and low evaluation accuracy after the service of advanced military aircraft. Firstly, the problem of field testability evaluation was described. Secondly, the hyperparameters in prior distribution of the testability parameters were obtained by combination of the moment equivalent method and the maximum entropy method based on the prior information. Finally, the posterior distribution was obtained by using Bayes formula, and the iterative estimation result of testability parameters was obtained. The practical case showed the correctness and advantages of the proposed method compared with the existing method. In addition, the prior information could be used effectively to improve accuracy of evaluation.

articleTitle: Analysis of Power Cycle Aging Test for SiC MOSFET
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Hangzhou)
abstract: Silicon carbide (SiC) metal-oxide-semiconductor field-effect transistors (MOSFETs) are gradually replacing silicon (Si)-based devices as the core devices for power conversion in high-temperature, high-pressure, and high-frequency applications due to their superior material properties. The long-term reliability of SiC MOSFETs has become a research focus. Power cycling tests, an important aging test for evaluating device reliability, can reflect the reliability under real working conditions to some extent. The test is conducted using a constant on/off time mode, and the on-state resistance and body diode voltage drop of the devices are measured online during the aging test. The experimental results show that an increase in on-state resistance during power cycling tests causes an increase in junction temperature, which leads to wire bond aging and eventually results in SiC MOSFET failure.

articleTitle: Railway Track Short-Wave Defect Identification Based on Axle Box Acceleration and Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Hangzhou)
abstract: Track welded joint impact and rail corrugation are common track short-wave defects in high-speed rail-way lines. Track short-wave defect inspection and analysis using vibration signals of vehicle dynamic response collected by axle box accelerators is relatively a proven technology, which is a great help of track health management. However, the real inspection data are pretty complicated. The accuracy of short-wave defect identification has much room for improvement. For deeper analysis of the characteristics of track short-wave defects and enhancing the quality of track health management, this paper pro-posed a new method for railway track short-wave defect identification from the perspective of real inspection data. Vehicle dynamic response vibration data are collected by a comprehensive inspection train and manually rechecked on site. By the on-site confirmation, typical samples of defects are integrated and divided into three categories: welded joint impacts, rail corrugations and non-defects. Signal processing approaches are applied to extract the features of those samples. The extracted features such as energy factor, crest factor, kurtosis, spectral entropy, etc. are input into a neural network for automatically learning and classifying. The results show that, by the combination of approaches of feature extraction and neural network, the impact defects and corrugations can be effectively identified from vehicle dynamic response vibration signals. Improving the quantity and quality of defect samples is the key point of identification accuracy enhancement. This method shows application prospects of axle box acceleration data mining and analysis of railway line health evolution.

articleTitle: Degradation Modeling Based on Polynomial Uncertain Process: a Case Study on Raliway Gyroscope
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Hangzhou)
abstract: Constructing an accurate performance degradation model is significant for analyzing equipment reliability and developing efficient maintenance strategies. In practical work scenarios, the available degradation data for equipment is often limited due to economic and technical constraints. This data contains a significant amount of epistemic uncertainty that cannot be adequately described by conventional probabilistic theories. To tackle this issue, this paper proposes a polynomial uncertain process within the framework of uncertainty theory to effectively characterize equipment's performance degradation. Compared to general linear or nonlinear uncertain processes, the polynomial uncertain process demonstrates the ability to accurately depict the degradation trajectories of equipment with different degradation characteristics at various stages. To estimate the unknown parameters of the polynomial uncertain process, this paper introduces a parameter estimation method based on the principles of least squares and minimum noise. Furthermore, the reliability of the equipment is analyzed and evaluated using the concepts of uncertainty theory and first hitting time. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method is illustrated in detail through an example involving a railway gyroscope.

articleTitle: Simulation and Calculation of Electrical Properties of Piezoelectric Ceramic Materials Na0.5Bi2.5Nb2O9under High-Temperature Irradiation Coupled Environment
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Hangzhou)
abstract: In order to study the electrical properties of piezoelectric ceramic materials under high-temperature irradiation coupled environment, the irradiation simulation model of Na<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.5</inf>Bi<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2.5</inf>Nb<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">9</inf>(NBN) piezoelectric ceramic materials was established using <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\gamma$</tex>-ray irradiation model and molecular dynamics model. The mechanical and electrical properties were studied at different temperatures of 300 K, 573 K, 755 K and 800 K and at different primary knock-on atoms (PKA) of 10 eV, 30 eV and 50 eV. The results show that the coupling of high temperature and high irradiation can produce more defects in the NBN piezoelectric ceramic material and affect the electrical properties of the material, which in turn leads to changes in the piezoelectric properties of the NBN piezoelectric ceramic material. Therefore, the simulation model established in this paper can be used to characterize the performance changes of NBN piezoelectric ceramic materials under the high-temperature irradiation coupling environment.

articleTitle: Helicopter Rotor Fault Diagnosis Based on IPSO and RVM
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Hangzhou)
abstract: To address the issue of low accuracy in traditional rotor fault diagnosis during the helicopter rotor fault diagnosis process, this paper presents a fault diagnosis method based on the Improved Particle Swarm Optimization (IPSO) algorithm for Relevance Vector Machine (RVM). The fitness function of the IPSO algorithm is defined as the mean squared error between the predicted classification results obtained through cross-validation and the actual classification. The IPSO algorithm is used to search for the optimal width factor of the RVM kernel function and establish the fault diagnosis model. Through simulation experiments and comparisons with Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) algorithm-based RVM and Improved Particle Swarm Optimization-based Support Vector Machine (SVM), it is demonstrated that this approach, compared to traditional rotor fault diagnosis methods, effectively improves the accuracy of fault recognition.

articleTitle: Combination of PSO and RF with Weights for Supervised Learning Model
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Hangzhou)
abstract: The pattern, path, and discrimination according to the data can automatically discovered by the mathematical models of machine learning (ML), and accordingly the outcomes are applied to project the prospects and/or cause decisions as stated by the brand-fresh, unseen data. The supervised learning (SL) makes whole solutions are identified while generating projects about the solution by gathering information based on the labeled data. The most popular SL method is random forests (RF) that is adaptable and may be used to solve both grouping and regression issues. The RF training procedure is lengthy, resource centralized, and prone to wrong group as a result of these and other drawbacks. In this context, a combination of particle swarm optimization (PSO) based on weighted RF is presented in order to improve the efficacy of the RF.

articleTitle: FFT-Driven Transformer Framework for Autonomous Underwater Vehicles Fault Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Hangzhou)
abstract: Deep learning has demonstrated notable proficiency in autonomous underwater vehicle (AUV) fault diagnosis applications. Nevertheless, the signals of AUVs working underwater are unstable and easily disturbed by noise, which makes it difficult for traditional deep-learning models to be applied to complex real-world scenarios. Therefore, it is crucial to overcome the impact of noise on feature extraction capabilities. To this end, this paper proposes an FFT-driven Transformer (FGF-Trans) framework for AUVs fault diagnosis. Specifically, the framework combines a frequency global filter block (FGF-Block) with a Transformer, which is able to capture the global contextual information of the entire feature instead of only local information. By virtue of this integration, the proposed framework can better extract fault feature information in noisy environments and exhibit excellent diagnostic accuracy. We experimentally validate the FGF-Trans method on the AUVs fault dataset. Experimental results show it has higher application potential and accuracy in actual scenarios than traditional deep learning models.

articleTitle: Slippage Analysis of Rolling Bearings with Various Profiles of Rolling Elements
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Hangzhou)
abstract: Rolling bearings play a crucial role in aerospace engine rotor systems by providing support to shafts, transmitting loads, and facilitating motion. A four-degree-of-freedom quasi-static analysis model, based on the Hertz elastic contact theory, is developed to examine the slip characteristics of cylindrical roller bearings. Comparative analysis reveals that, under different operating conditions, an increase in radial load leads to a gradual reduction in cage slip rate. The initial speed of the inner ring has minimal impact on bearing behavior during steady-state operation, but as the speed rises, the cage slip rate gradually increases. Additionally, essential structural parameters like the number of rollers and radial clearance significantly influence the bearing performance. Notably, different roller profiles result in substantial variations in the performance of roller bearings, necessitating their design and usage in engineering applications based on practical considerations.

articleTitle: Gearbox Fault Diagnosis Based on the Ratio of Characteristic Energy
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Hangzhou)
abstract: The kurtosis index in resonance demodulation technology is vulnerable to random and unexpected period impulsiveness. To overcome this drawback, a novel criterion named the ratio of characteristic energy (RCE) is proposed in this paper to detect the gearbox fault with the help of the fast kurtogram method. Firstly, signal is decomposed into a series of sub-signals with different bandwidths. Then each sub-signal is analyzed by square envelope spectrum (SES) technology. And the SES is transformed into energy by square operation. Then, each amplitude of the fault characteristic and its harmonics are summed. Therefore, RCE is calculated by the ratio of the sum of characteristic energy and the total energy. Finally, the optimal resonance demodulation bandwidth is determined by maxing RCE. Signal from gearbox with sun gear wear fault is applied to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method. Furthermore, the superiority of it is shown by comparing with the existing work.

Author Keywords: Resonance Demodulation; Fast Kurtogram; Index; The ratio of characteristic energy; Gearbox

articleTitle: An Analysis Method of System Safety Requirements Based on Usage Scenario
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Hangzhou)
abstract: based on the traditional security requirement analysis method, combined with the MBSE model and the task scenario model, the scenario-based system security requirement analysis method is studied. Through the task activity function composition of the equipment, the fault logic relationship of the system and equipment is analyzed. On this basis, the requirement including the function failure probability is formed The security requirements of a device or system, such as operational requirements

articleTitle: Agent-Based Contrastive Domain Generalization for Fault Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Hangzhou)
abstract: Data-driven fault diagnosis plays a core role in intelligent operations and maintenance in modern industries. In practice, the deployment of fault diagnosis models often takes place in highly dynamic working environments. Consequently, models trained on a specific working environment may not generalize well to data from different working environments (i.e., different distributions). The naive approach of training a new model for each new working environment is impractical. Contrastive learning emerges as a promising solution, aiming to learn domain-invariant embeddings by leveraging rich semantic relationships among samples from different domains. A simple strategy involves pulling positive sample pairs from different regions closer together while pushing negative sample pairs further apart. However, aligning positive pairs across different domains often hinders model generalization due to significant distribution discrepancies. To address this challenge, we propose an Agent-based Contrastive Domain Generalization (ACDG) approach for diagnosing rotating machinery faults. Specifically, our method replaces the original sample-level relationships with agent-level relationships, effectively alleviating the issue of positive alignment. Experimental results demonstrate that our proposed ACDG method outperforms state-of-the-art approaches on four real-world fault diagnosis datasets. The favorable performance of ACDG on new unseen target domains contributes to more practical data-driven methods operating in challenging real-world environments.

articleTitle: Early Fault Feature Extraction Based on Improved 2.5-Dimensional Envelope Spectrum
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Hangzhou)
abstract: Owing to the small transient pulses in the early fault signal, particularly in the presence of strong background noise that interferes with the detection of shocks, the efficient extraction of the fault characteristics of rolling bearings is challenging. To facilitate better extraction of the bearing fault information at early stages, this study proposes a modified 2.5-dimensional (2.5D) envelope spectral fault feature extraction method. As higher-order cumulants are still affected by noise in practice, this study improves the 2.5D cumulants to better eliminate Gaussian noise. Subsequently, the improved 2.5D spectrum is combined with a spectrum envelope to extract the characteristics of the bearing fault signals, and the information entropy is introduced to evaluate the parameter values. Experimental data show that the improved 2.5D envelope spectrum better extract the bearing fault information than the 1.5-dimensional and 2.5D spectral methods. Thus, the proposed method offers certain advantages in terms of fault signal extraction

articleTitle: Investigation on Wear Diagnosis of Aero-Engine Mechanical System Based on Lubricant Wear Particle Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Hangzhou)
abstract: To improve the accuracy of mechanical system wear diagnosis in aero-engines, this paper extracts characteristic parameters such as size, color, and texture from wear particle images, constructs a correlation between wear particle characteristic parameters and wear types, and forms a typical wear particle database. Based on neural networks, an intelligent identification method for wear particle types is established, and the accuracy of wear particle identification is discussed. The results show that the identification accuracy of normal wear particles, spherical wear particles, and cutting wear particles can exceed 85%. After improvement through hierarchical, parameter addition, and multiple method fusion, the identification accuracy of fatigue wear particles and sliding wear particles has been significantly improved, and the identification accuracy can exceed 80%.

articleTitle: Application of Continuous Wavelet Transform and Statistical Process Control Chart in Gear Health State Assessment
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Hangzhou)
abstract: Timely detection of gear faults is of great significance for improving equipment operating efficiency and economic benefits. Firstly, the original vibration data of the gearbox is subjected to continuous wavelet transform analysis. Subsequently, typical signals within one rotation period of the gear are extracted based on time synchronous averaging. Secondly, a vector autoregressive model is used to model the healthy data and obtain the residuals of the overall dataset. Furthermore, the residual data were used to extract characteristic parameters that can reflect the progressive degradation of gears. Subsequently, the T<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> control chart and cumulative sum (CUSUM) chart were utilized to identify the health status of gears. Different applicable conditions for each control chart were analyzed, as well as appropriate analysis of different parameters. The research results demonstrate that using the T<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> control chart can more precisely point the occurrence of faults at data file number 14 and 71, thus, the effectiveness and advantages of statistical process control chart in detecting gear health status are affirmed.

articleTitle: Fault Diagnosis of Aircraft Landing Gear Retractable System Based on BO-SVM
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Hangzhou)
abstract: In response to the problems of poor recognition accuracy and low speed in traditional machine learning algorithms for fault diagnosis of aircraft landing gear retraction and retraction systems, a fault diagnosis method for landing gear retraction and retraction systems is proposed on the basis of the analysis of the landing gear retraction and retraction system model, which combines Bayesian optimization with support vector machines. By analyzing the structure and function of the landing gear retraction and retraction system, an AMESim model of the landing gear retraction and retraction system is established to obtain fault simulation data; the key feature quantity is extracted from the original data by combining the time-domain feature and frequency-domain feature, and normalized to obtain the standard model input data; Relying on Bayesian optimization's efficient, flexible, and precise optimization ability to find the optimal penalty factor and kernel function of support vector machines; Through simulation experiments and comparative analysis with various faults diagnosis algorithms, the results show that this algorithm has high accuracy and fast diagnostic speed, verifying the superiority of BO-SVM. It can achieve fault diagnosis for landing gear retraction and retraction systems and has maybe of value to the engineering.

Author Keywords: Landing gear retraction and retraction system

articleTitle: A Pretrained Significant Sample Generator for Partial Domain Transfer in Rotating Machinery Bearing Fault Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Hangzhou)
abstract: In the context of bearing fault diagnosis, traditional supervised models often struggle due to a lack of sufficient information under novel operational conditions. Transfer learning is designed to address this issue by mitigating the domain shift between the source and target domains, thereby enhancing the utilization of the information available in the source domain. Furthermore, partial domain transfer learning addresses the problem of label imbalance, where the target domain has fewer labels than the source domain. Nevertheless, these methods generally presume the availability of a sufficiently large and balanced sample size, an assumption that often proves challenging in reality. For instance, when machinery faults occur, operations are usually terminated immediately. This results in the target domain being left with inadequate sample sizes, thereby inducing a sample imbalance between the two domains. To address the problem of sample imbalance in partial domain transfer scenarios, this paper proposes a pre-trained significance sample generator. This generator employs the backbone network to identify secure samples within the target domain, which are then used to augment the dataset of that domain. This process not only prevents mode collapse but also rectifies the sample imbalance. Experimental results validate the effectiveness of this generator in resolving the sample imbalance problem in the context of partial domain transfer bearing fault diagnosis.

articleTitle: A Wear Debris Detection Method Based on Sparse Decomposition
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Hangzhou)
abstract: A debris detection method for oil monitoring is proposed for the triple-coils inductive sensor. Regarding the high false alarms rate in the detection results, time domain analysis is carried out firstly to enhance the difference between debris signatures and noise signatures, in which signal energy is selected as the most effective index. Hereafter, a sliding window with fixed width is added to the signal energy values, in which sparse decomposition is performed and the potential debris signatures are determined. The evaluation criteria is the ratio of the energy of potential debris signature to the total energy within the sliding window. Signatures exceeding the threshold are considered as debris signatures. The monitoring data comes from the test runs of an aero engine of a type, all the debris are detected successfully even if one of them appears during the change in working condition. In summary, this method shows satisfactory results in both detection accuracy and the inhibition of false alarms. Moreover, it is applicable for signals from various sensing principles, including but not limited to the inductance, since the detection performance is only related to the signal itself.

articleTitle: A Standard Self-Learning Unsupervised Contrastive Learning Model for Bearing Fault Diagnosis in Imbalanced Datasets
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Hangzhou)
abstract: Deep learning is widely employed in rolling bearing fault diagnosis due to its powerful feature extraction capability. However, deep learning heavily relies on balanced datasets, and the number of samples for fault categories in actual detected data is much smaller than that of normal categories, which significantly reduces the performance of deep learning models for fault diagnosis. To address this issue, this article proposes an unsupervised contrastive learning phase method based on standard self‑learning data augmentation (SSDA-USCL). Firstly, positive and negative sample pairs are constructed through SSDA. Secondly, feature extraction of sample pairs is achieved through unsupervised comparative learning (USCL). Finally, cross-entropy with optimized weight is utilized to classify samples. Experiments were conducted on the CWRU dataset according to the proposed method in this article and results showed that it can learn distinct discriminative features in imbalanced datasets with high diagnostic accuracy.

articleTitle: Research on Coal Mine Multi-stage Drainage System Coordination Control Strategy
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Hangzhou)
abstract: The underground drainage system of coal mine undertakes the important task of discharging underground surge water, which is the key link to ensure the safe production of the mine. In order to cope with the difficulties of upper and lower level coordination, low pump operation efficiency, high energy consumption and other problems brought about by the deep mining of drainage system, this paper firstly establishes a mathematical model of multi-stage drainage system, solves the systematic search for the optimal solution space by using mixed integer programming, proposes the optimal control strategy for the operation of pumps at all levels, and achieves the maximization of system economic benefits under the comprehensive consideration of peak avoidance and valley filling mode. Finally, in order to verify the effectiveness of the method, a coal mine secondary drainage system is selected as a case study object, and simulation is carried out to verify the data through its historical working conditions, and the experimental simulation results show that: the implementation of the coordinated control strategy of the multi-stage drainage system in terms of energy consumption, economic benefits have been significantly improved, and provide a theoretical basis for the sustainable development and efficient operation of the drainage system of coal mines.

Author Keywords: mixed integer programming;avoid peaks and fill valleys

articleTitle: GUI-Based Multi-Objective Maintenance Optimization of Series-Parallel Pipeline Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Hangzhou)
abstract: It is necessary to establish a maintenance management framework that can be broadly applied to the pipeline systems with different structures, so as to provide a reference for the maintenance of industrial pipelines. For series-parallel pipeline systems, this paper develops a graphical user interface (GUI) that can be used to balance the tradeoff between transport continuity and maintenance costs. Thus, reasonable and reliable maintenance solutions for pipeline systems are provided. The interface allows the input of field inspection data to develop multiple maintenance strategies that focus on different optimization metrics for management to choose from. The effectiveness of the operational results is verified by case analysis. The developed interface can be subsequently improved not only algorithmically, but also in terms of the interface framework to increase the possibility and universality of its application in theoretical research and industry applications.

articleTitle: Fault Diagnosis of Planetary Gearbox in Nuclear Circulating Water Pump-Unit Under Heavy Background Noise
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Hangzhou)
abstract: The traditional one-dimensional Convolutional neural network is difficult to realize adaptive attention to fault characteristics, resulting in lower accuracy and generalization ability of the network model. In order to solve the problem, this paper proposes a hybrid multi attention network model (HMA1DCNN) that includes channel attention mechanism (CAM), time attention mechanism (TAM), and multi-scale attention mechanism (MSAM). The model is validated using a planetary gearbox gear and bearing fault dataset from a circulating water pump (CRF) unit test bench. The results show that the model can accurately classify different health states of planetary gearboxes under strong noise backgrounds. Compared with other models, the accuracy of fault identification has been improved.

articleTitle: Multi-source Vibration Signals Fusion-Based Condition Assessment of Francis Turbine Unit under Complex Operating Conditions
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Hangzhou)
abstract: Francis turbine units (FTUs) operate under complex conditions and gradually deteriorate during their service life. Information about operating characteristics is indirectly contained in the monitoring vibration signal of the FTUs. However, the influence of operating conditions on vibration characteristics is usually not considered in vibration data cleaning for FTUs. Furthermore, existing unit condition assessment methods require the construction of a health mapping model between operating condition parameters and unit vibration signals. Analysis of single-source vibration signals alone makes it difficult to comprehensively and reliably evaluate unit condition. In this paper, a multi-source vibration signals fusion-based condition assessment of FTUs under complex operating conditions is proposed. Firstly, the sparse spectrum Gaussian process regression method is introduced to establish a probability fitting model of the operating condition-vibration amplitude, calculate the deviation index between working head, power and the vibration distribution under different operating conditions. And then the K-Means++ clustering method based on the deviation index is designed to achieve anomaly data cleaning. Secondly, taking into account the coupling relationship between the operating condition parameters and the multisource vibration signals, a multisource vibration-operating condition correlation health model based on dual-channel convolutional auto-encoder is proposed. Furthermore, by integrating the degradation information of multi-source vibration signals, a comprehensive degradation index is constructed to comprehensively quantify the degradation state of the Francis turbine unit. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method is validated through a set of on-site measured data from a large-scale hydropower station.

articleTitle: Imbalanced Fault Diagnosis Based on Supervised Prototypical Contrastive Network
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Hangzhou)
abstract: In recent years, data-driven methods have found extensive application in mechanical fault diagnosis. However, these methods have demonstrated a tendency to become overly reliant on having a sufficient amount of labeled fault data. In real-world industrial scenarios, mechanical equipment often operates under normal conditions, leading to an abundance of normal data but a scarcity of fault data. To address this issue, we propose a novel supervised prototypical contrastive network (SPCN) for imbalanced fault diagnosis. To mitigate the data imbalance problem, we introduce a data augmentation method called Mixup to generate additional fault data, thereby reducing the imbalance ratio. Subsequently, we estimate each class prototype based on these augmented fault data, and then, through the minimization of the supervised prototypical contrastive loss, we enhance the intra-class compactness and learn class-wise discriminative features. Additionally, we apply mutual information maximization to ensure the reliability of the predicted results. To evaluate the effectiveness and superiority of our proposed method under different imbalance ratios, we conduct experiments using a bearing dataset.

articleTitle: Intelligent Fault Diagnosis Method of Rolling Bearing Based on Active Learning Under Unbalanced Samples
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Hangzhou)
abstract: For the problem of low fault diagnosis accuracy of rolling bearings under unbalanced samples, we propose an intelligent fault diagnosis method of rolling bearings based on active learning. Firstly, data features are extracted from rolling bearing signals in both the time domain and time frequency domain according to the running sample to realize the feature representation of sample. Secondly, a Gaussian mixture model undersampling method with sample characteristics is proposed, and the weight coefficient of the model is obtained through training to realize the same distribution extraction of samples in multiple types, and solve the problem of sample imbalance. Thirdly, an active learning classifier is established based on density peak clustering method, which is then utilized for fault diagnosis of unlabelled samples. Finally, the proposed method is validated by the simulation test sample of rolling bearing fault. The results show that, compared with the comparison methods, the proposed method can effectively improve the problem of low fault diagnosis accuracy caused by sample imbalance.

articleTitle: Lithium battery state of health prediction method based on online knee point warning identification of coupling temperature
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Hangzhou)
abstract: The capacity of lithium-ion batteries degrades rapidly after the knee point, which means that early warning before the knee point is more important for the continued safe use of the battery. This paper proposes a dynamic early identification knee point warning framework. Pearson correlation analysis and mutual information are used to prove the dependence between temperature and incremental capacity. Copula-Based Outlier Detection is used to evaluate the coupling effect. Moving T test is used to determine the knee point warning. Secondly, the similar knee point warning batteries under similar charging and discharging conditions are searched in the cloud database, so as to train the Gaussian process regression prediction model. In this paper, a total of 30 batteries are used. The knee point warning appears 15.12% earlier than the knee point on average, and the average root mean square error of the state of health prediction result is as low as 0.76%.

articleTitle: An Informer-LSTM Network for State-of-Charge Estimation of Lithium-Ion Batteries
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Hangzhou)
abstract: In this paper, we propose an Informer-LSTM hybrid model for lithium-ion battery state of charge (SOC) estimation. The Informer-LSTM model combines the strengths of the Informer model and Long short-term memory model to effectively capture the temporal dependencies and position features of the input data. By employing a sliding window mechanism, the long original data is divided into overlapping shorter segments, enabling the model to retain the relative time characteristics. The proposed model predicts multiple future SOC values at each time step, providing a comprehensive understanding of the battery's dynamic behavior. Extensive experiments are conducted on various charging/discharging modes and different temperature conditions. The results demonstrate that the model exhibits excellent generalization capability, with the majority of the tested data achieving root mean square error and mean absolute error of less than 1% in charging/discharging modes and temperatures not included in the training set. Furthermore, our model outperforms LSTM in terms of training speed, estimation accuracy, and generalization ability. Overall, our proposed model contributes to the advancement of SOC estimation and paves the way for realtime applications in practical settings.

articleTitle: Research on Fault Diagnosis Technology for Unstructured Data Oriented Avionics Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Hangzhou)
abstract: In response to the fault diagnosis requirements of unstructured text data in avionics systems, this article establishes a text classification model through text preprocessing, feature selection, and text representation, and classifies the text test set to achieve fault diagnosis of unstructured text data in avionics systems. This article studies the classification and diagnosis of avionics system fault description texts based on classification algorithms such as naive Bayesian classification, K-nearest neighbor classification, SVM classification, LDA model, etc. This article collected unstructured text data from 1500 avionics system fault descriptions, and validated and analyzed the text classification fault diagnosis algorithm proposed in this article. The fault diagnosis efficiency was significantly improved, and the diagnostic accuracy was high. This article proposes a classification method for unstructured data in avionics systems, which can provide reference for maintenance personnel, provide a basis for management decision-making of avionics maintenance organizations, and improve the maintenance quality of avionics systems.

articleTitle: A Digital Failure Twin Model For PHM: From Concepts To Maturity Levels
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Hangzhou)
abstract: In the context of industry 4.0, traditional reliability engineering has the opportunity to greatly benefit from the big data generated by Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) and the advancement of industrial intelligence technologies. To make full use of the opportunities emerging in the era of industry 4.0, a Digital Failure Twin (DFT) is proposed as a dynamic virtual modeling framework that encompasses various dimensions such as model, data, connection, and computation. This framework is designed to simulate and forecast the failure behavior of complex real-world systems throughout their entire life cycle, enhancing Prognostics and Health Management (PHM) application, ultimately leading to improved reliability, safety, and operational efficiency. Five maturity levels of a DFT model are defined to support the development and implementation of DFT in practice. This evolution entails transitioning from static failure modeling based on historical data to dynamic predictive maintenance capabilities integrated with artificial intelligence. The potential application of the DFT framework on prognostics and health management is also discussed. Through the discussion, we show that introducing the DFT in prognostics and health management could improve operational and maintenance planning and reduce failure occurrence, as the framework could provide an accurate and up-to-date prediction of the evolution of the failure behavior.

articleTitle: ConDa-CorA: A Context-and-Data-driven Correlation Analysis Mechanism for Complex System's Multi-Senor Time-series Anomaly Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Hangzhou)
abstract: Correlation analysis plays an important role in the multi-sensor time-series treatment, such as anomaly detection and time-series prediction. However, the common-accepted methods are almost based on pure statistical mechanism, which risks of suspicious correlation while analyzing the variously-interrelated data of industrial systems. Meanwhile, the contextual knowledge, such as the industrial documentation, is another valuable source which can deduce the physical or structural correlations among the parameters and thus, provides a complementary valuable perspective on correlations among industrial parameters. In this paper, we propose a context-and-data-driven correlation analysis (ConDa-CorA) mechanism for multi-sensor parameters' correlation analysis, which is constructed in a general industrial application condition. Firstly, the proposed method builds a keyword-oriented semantic analysis module, which takes advantage of contextual knowledge represented by the parameters' brief descriptions to achieve a semantic correlation correspondent to some physical-or-structural relations. Secondly, a repeatability-based statistical analysis is integrated to ensure a more robust correlation mining on the operating correlation via the statistical knowledge, particularly accumulated data. Finally, an evidence combination method based on evidence theory is proposed to combine the semantic and the statistical correlations respectively based on the contextual and the statistical knowledges and improve therefore the representability of the mined correlation coefficients. Experiments on a public ALFA UAV control dataset are conducted, by which the proposed hybrid method is demonstrated to achieve state-of-the-art results on its effectivity on anomaly detection task.

articleTitle: Spare Parts Varieties Optimization for Hydraulic System Using Data Envelopment Analysis Method
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Hangzhou)
abstract: Hydraulic system is a complex system with electromechanical-hydraulic coupling, so the relationship between components and the system should be considered when determining the variety of spare parts. In view of the problems that the complexity of the designed functional structure and the harm degree of failure mode can't be given directly, we obtain the severity, criticality and other important parameters related to the system of all the least replaceable units through the results of Failure Mode, Effects and Criticality Analysis (FMECA). An index system focusing on FMECA results is proposed in terms of product life-cycle process. Then, the method of FMECA for hydraulic system is briefly introduced. A spares optimization model for hydraulic system is proposed based on data envelopment analysis with the constraints of 12 factors of the index system. A case study is given to illustrate the proposed method. The theoretical base was provided by model to decide spare parts varieties for hydraulic system effectively.

articleTitle: Reconstruction of Non-Uniform Strain Along FBG Based on Dynamic Particle Swarm Optimization
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Hangzhou)
abstract: Aircraft structural health monitoring is an important development direction of PHM technology. In order to understand the non-uniform strain distribution of the wing for condition monitoring, a dynamic particle swarm optimization (DPSO) algorithm for retrieving the non-uniform strain field of FBG is proposed in this paper. The algorithm uses the transfer matrix method to calculate the reflection intensity spectrum of the non-uniform strain and optimizes the strain profile by using the calculated reflection spectrum. In order to accelerate the convergence speed of PSO and avoid falling into local optimal solutions, dynamic inertia weights are used. The reconstruction accuracy of DPSO and PSO is measured for linear, higher-order and sinusoidal strain distributions. Finally, an experimental study is carried out on the cantilever beam with deflection, and the results of reconstruction are compared with those of finite element analysis. The effectiveness of DPSO algorithm and reflection spectrum for non-uniform strain reconstruction is verified, which provides a possibility for using non-uniform strain information to monitor the condition of wing structure.

articleTitle: Deep Learning for Wafer Map Defect Detection: A Review
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Hangzhou)
abstract: Wafer defect recognition is a critical task in semiconductor manufacturing, as the detection and early identification of defects can significantly impact yield and product quality. Various inspection methods are employed to detect defects on semiconductor wafers, and traditional approaches often involve manual inspection by domain experts. However, these methods are time-consuming, labor-intensive, and prone to errors due to the complexity of wafer images. As a result, computer-aided methods have gained traction to alleviate human burden and reduce errors caused by fatigue and subjective differences. In recent years, deep learning has emerged as a powerful approach for wafer defect recognition. Its hierarchical architecture enables the extraction of high-level features, and its strong feature extraction capabilities contribute to accurate defect classification. Recent studies have shown that deep learning algorithms can achieve higher accuracy and efficiency than manual classification by experts. This review article systematically examines the application of deep learning in wafer defect recognition, focusing on four typical algorithms: autoencoders, convolutional neural networks (CNNs), generative adversarial networks (GANs), and recurrent neural networks (RNNs). The mechanisms, developments, and applications of these algorithms are introduced. Subsequently, their applications in wafer defect recognition are comprehensively reviewed, highlighting their strengths and limitations. Finally, looking ahead, the potential for further development of deep learning in wafer defect recognition is promising. Future research could explore more complex architectures, opening new avenues for real-time and efficient defect detection applications.

articleTitle: RUL Prediction Architecture of Rolling Bearing Considering Failure Behavior Determination
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Hangzhou)
abstract: Remaining useful life (RUL) prediction is a significant part of prognostics and health management. Recently, intelligent data-driven methods of deep learning methods and transfer learning methods for RUL prediction have become mainstream. However, they still mostly suffer from some limitations: 1) failure behavior determination (FBD) was not considered to enhance the prediction precision during the RUL prediction process. 2) The health threshold for initial degradation timepoint (IDT) was set with the help of health indicator (HI) values during the stable operation stage. To address the above drawbacks, a novel RUL prediction architecture of rolling bearing considering FBD is proposed. First, First, a relative HI (RHI) construction method by the improved grey target decision (IGTD) is proposed to reduce the differences of health state during the stable operation stage and then IDT and FBD can be determined based on the proposed RHI. Second, to enhance the prediction precision, a novel RUL prediction ConvLSTM architecture considering FBD is proposed. Finally, one case of run-to-failure test data are used to verify the feasibility and superiority of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Wind Power Fault Detection Based on Vertical Federated Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Hangzhou)
abstract: Wind power generation is one of the most widely used distributed renewable energy sources. The diagnosis and monitoring of wind power system is one of the important means to ensure its power supply reliability. Since wind power monitoring data is an important production data for enterprises, how to realize distributed diagnosis of wind power system under the premise of ensuring data security is a difficult problem that needs to be solved. To solve the above problems, this paper proposes a new vertical Federated learning method to achieve distributed fault diagnosis of wind power systems on the premise of ensuring data privacy and security. The method was verified through testing of EDP, NERL and other real-time wind power data, and the highest diagnostic accuracy reached more than 99%, showing its great potential to be used in this field.

articleTitle: Research on Fault Diagnosis Method of Solid-State Power Controller of Rocket
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Hangzhou)
abstract: Considering the scarcity of test nodes in solid-state power controller (SSPC) circuits, the challenges in acquiring fault data, and the frequent misdiagnoses and omissions by traditional algorithms, this study presents an SSPC circuit fault diagnosis method underpinned by a particle swarm optimized extreme learning machine (PSO-ELM) algorithm. This enhanced algorithm markedly boosts the accuracy and efficiency of fault diagnosis. Through the simulation of the electrical-thermal coupling effect, the actual operational conditions of the SSPC circuit are accurately mirrored. Feature values extracted from the temperature data during the circuit's power-up to stable operation process serve as the diagnostic model's input parameters. A PSO-ELM model is then established to optimize the input weights and hidden layer bias, thereby refining and enhancing the model, while elevating the diagnostic accuracy of the SSPC circuit. Experimental results affirm that the enhanced algorithm effectively improves fault diagnosis accuracy.

Author Keywords: particle swarm optimized extreme learning machine (PSO-ELM)

articleTitle: How to Choose Proper Prognostic Knowledge and Transfer It ? A New Deep Sub-domain Adversarial Adaptation Method for Few-shot Remaining Useful Life Prediction Based on Wavelet Scattering Network
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Hangzhou)
abstract: With huge success in remaining useful life (RUL) prediction of different rotatory machines, deep transfer learning techniques generally require sufficient source domain data to extract prognostic knowledge and to transfer them as well. In practical applications, however, it is not easy to accumulate enough run-to-failure degradation data from source domain for model training. To guarantee the transfer effect, two concerns intuitively rise up: what prognostic knowledge can be transferred, and, how to transfer it? To address these concerns, a deep sub-domain adversarial adaptation method is proposed for RUL prediction in few-shot environment. With the merit of wavelet scattering network (WSN) in expanding feature space, a complete feature set is first constructed for the few-shot whole-life degradation data by applying WSN with different frequency bands (decomposition scales) and rotation orientations. An orientation-first selection strategy is further built to determine the optimal orientation features in all scales, with sub-domains divided by different scales in source domain and target domain. Second, a new frequency contribution indicator (FCI) is designed in terms of geometric similarity to quantify the contribution of each frequency band to the transfer process. Finally, for the sub-source domain and sub-target domain at the same scale, a deep sub-domain adversarial network is built orderly with the domain discriminator weighted by FCI. The selective transfer of prognostic knowledge is then achieved. Experiments are conducted on a widely-used bearing dataset IEEE PHM Challenge 2012. The results demonstrate that the selective transfer from different frequency bands is beneficial to improve RUL prediction performance in few-shot environment. The results also prove that the orientation information of wavelet feature performs more critical than the scale information in the transfer process.

articleTitle: Analysis of Fatigue Crack Propagation Law and Fault Characteristics on the Outer Edge of Aeroengine Compressor Disk
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Hangzhou)
abstract: The expansion of crack in aeroengine disk to a certain extent can lead to sudden disk rupture, which is a serious fault that may lead to major safety accidents. The impact of disk cracks on shaft vibration is weak, so it is difficult to detect through monitoring shaft vibration. However, they induce regular vibrations of nearby blades. Therefore, the study of the influence of cracks on blade tips” vibration characteristics can provide a theoretical basis for online monitoring and fault diagnosis of disk cracks. In this study, a blisk analysis model was established based on a certain type of aeroengine rotor system. Firstly, the propagation path of cracks is studied, and it can guide us on what kind of cracks to be implanted at the outer edge of disk. Considering the influence of the position and angle of the initial crack on the crack propagation path, it was found that the position of the crack played a major role. And the crack will deflect towards the nearest blade. Secondly, the natural frequencies and blade tip spacing of the disk with different cracks of different depths were studied. The results indicate that the influence of disk cracks on low-order modes is relatively small. But as the depth of the crack increases, the influence on the natural frequency of the dominant mode of the disk gradually increases. Disk with cracks is more prone to exciting blade-disk coupled vibrations. Disk cracks can cause regular changes in blade tip spacing. The blade tip spacing curve near the crack looks like a slightly deformed “W” character. Comparing the above situation with the crack on the blade, it was found that cracks on the blades caused the blade spacing curve to resemble a “Z” character tilted to the left. The differences are distinct, and it is easy to differentiate between the two cracks based on blade tip spacing.

articleTitle: Research on Sampling and Life Prediction of Storage Products Based on Uncertainty Theory
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Reliability and Prognostics and Health Management Conference (PHM-Hangzhou)
abstract: Products with the characteristics of “long-term storage, small amount of testing, once-used” are called storage products. For the characteristics and engineering requirements of storage products, this paper proposes a quantum clustering-based sampling method for storage products. First, this paper selects a series of evaluation indexes under the framework of evaluation index system from four perspectives. Secondly, experienced experts were selected to score the selected indicators. Then, the uncertainty consensus model is used to process the scores of several experts, which reduces the large amount of epistemic uncertainty due to the small sample information. Third, the quantum clustering algorithm is introduced for the division of sampling matrices, and a sampling method is established for sample extraction. Finally, the practicality and operability of the sampling method of this paper are verified by taking a storage product as an example. It provides a new method for small sample sampling of storage products with epistemic uncertainty, and improves the accuracy of storage product reliability evaluation to a certain extent.
